newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Bonds see-sawed in a tight eight-point range on Monday in what dealers described as a thin, jobber-driven day's trade.

After initially moving to a high of 14.895 percent in the morning session, the R150 moved to 14.82 percent in the afternoon before returning to 14.85 at 1400 GMT -- little changed from Friday's 14.86 level.
Dealers linked the morning's weakness to the general strike called by the Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu).
An estimated 40,000 people marched through central Johannesburg on Monday to protest new labour laws, while Cosatu said two million workers country-wide had heeded its one-day general strike call.
"The jobbers were a bit nervous about the march and sold some stock," a trader said.

But jobbers bought back that stock later as the march passed without incident and as the U.S. Treasury bond extended two consecutive days of gains at the end of last week to a third session in early New York trade.
Much of the focus on the day, however, was on May gold and foreign exchange reserves data, which the Reserve Bank will release at 1600 GMT.
A consensus poll of economists called for a 3.3 billion rand rise in the headline figure to 17.7 billion rand, although traders said there was some talk the figure would be better.
"If it's a good figure, we should move a bit firmer tomorrow," a dealer said, noting however that technical resistance was likely to prove tough to crack at 14.80 percent.
On the foreign exchange market the rand edged sideways in equally lacklustre trade.
The rand was last quoted at 4.4715/4745 against the dollar from 4.4700/4730 on Friday.
"It's been very quiet. We opened at 4.47 the figure, saw a London-based bank try to buy it up, but they were capped at 4.4730 where other London guys sold dollars," a trader said.
Local importer demand also surfaced in the morning session. Traders said the London-based demand had been triggered by concerns about the Cosatu strike, preferring to go into the day long dollars.
But offshore dollar selling as well as exporter supply stymied any attempts the currency made at probing beyond the 4.4730 area, they said.
Traders noted that the rand had largely shrugged off the dollar's rally against the mark and yen, although the U.S. unit's strength was likely to be a factor on the market on Tuesday.

However, the rand did score against the crosses to last trade at 0.3859/3862 marks from 0.3805/3810 on Friday and at 26.0237/0635 yen from 25.9736/26.013 yen previously. Against sterling, the rand was last quoted at 7.2985/3058 from 7.3250/3344.
On the money market, three-month NCD rates remained unchanged from Friday at 16.35 percent offered, as did 90-day BA rates at 15.85 percent.
South Africa's money market shortage rose to 6.622 billion rand on Saturday from 6.396 billion rand on Friday, the Reserve Bank said.
